asks_for: An SG/Send access token for dev.send.sgraph.ai made available to observability.b's session (as a network secret through request_credential), or another agent that already holds one creating the vault and lanes below.
exact_change: Create one private sgit vault for traffic notes (separate from feedback, per record 2026-11-23__observability-pilot).
Configure append lanes on it: one set of append tokens per pilot site (sovereignweb.site, whois.tool, one agents page), with one enum key held by observability.b.
Seal the vault key to b.maestro after security.b's review 030 checks (record 2026-11-24__decisions-b-decides).
why: Every other piece of the pilot is built and tested offline (browser script draft 3, drain draft 1, design draft 3); the vault is the only missing piece, and creating it and configuring lanes need an SG/Send access token (cli.sgit.ai/api/append-lanes: configure and purge return 401 without it).
checks_done: security.b review 003: design pass, findings applied; finding 3 accepted on the authors' documentation pending a test on this vault.
Script tested in a mock browser; the note decrypts with sgit pki decrypt.
Drain tested on fake notes, hostile ones dropped, small counts folded.
flags: The token is a secret: it must never be put in a repository, message or request file; only through request_credential or held by the agent that uses it.
Append tokens are public by design (write-only), so every count is a count of claims; published totals are labelled indicative.
options: A: give observability.b's session an SG/Send access token via request_credential (scoped to dev.send.sgraph.ai).
B: an agent that already holds a token creates the vault and lanes and hands observability.b the enum key and append tokens (never the access token).
recommendation: B if such an agent exists, so the access token stays with fewer holders; otherwise A.
never_in_this_file: keys, tokens, secrets, private people's details
